native_result.query: In which century do Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form show opposite growth trends for the first time, with Pottery Decoration increasing significantly and Pottery Form declining simultaneously?
native_result.HypoA: In 1700 BCE, for the first time, Diversity in Pottery Decoration shows a significant increase while Diversity in Pottery Form experiences a notable decline. This marks a unique divergence in the growth trends of these two cultural capital variables.
native_result.HypoB: Pottery Decoration diversity and Pottery Form diversity first move in opposite directions in the century 1700-1600 BCE (century beginning CE -1700; Late Neolithic, capital.csv group = LN), at the step from the preceding century 1800 BCE (CE -1800). There Pottery Decoration (Zkeverz / PotteryDecoration_inter) rises significantly from Z = -0.48 to Z = +0.97 (Delta = +1.45 Z, +0.0145 Z/yr, 3.5 sd of its own century-to-century change distribution), while Pottery Form (ZKeform / PotteryForm_inter) simultaneously falls from Z = +0.74 to Z = -1.13 (Delta = -1.87 Z, -0.0187 Z/yr, 3.4 sd) - a 3.32 Z opposite-signed swing and the largest of all 38 century-to-century transitions (rank 1/38; bivariate Mahalanobis distance 5.89, empirical p ~ 0.026). It is the FIRST such century: none of the 25 earlier transitions from 4300 BCE onward satisfies the rule and none comes close - on every earlier century where decoration rose, form did not decline at all (closest +0.01 Z at 2200 BCE), and on every earlier century where form declined, decoration did not rise (closest -0.04 Z at 2000 BCE). The event is a genuine direction reversal for form (+0.15 to -1.87) plus a ~13-fold acceleration of an existing decoration increase, and is unanimous across all 12 design variants (both time bases, magnitude thresholds 0.05-0.5 Z, 0.5/1 sd thresholds, tie-inclusive rule); the only other partially qualifying century is 1000 BCE, 700 years later (Delta Dec +0.56 with form flat at its floor), so 'first' is unambiguous. Under the alternative convention naming the earlier endpoint of the transition the same event is 1800 BCE (CE -1800); smoothing/acceleration constructions spread the apparent onset over 1800-1600 BCE and are onset-lag diagnostics only. Because PotteryForm sits at its floor value (-1.13) in 16 of 39 centuries and both series show long exact plateaus (13 of 38 transitions are no-change for both), the defensible claim is about within-series change rather than absolute diversity or cross-series level comparison, and the fall of PotteryForm to the floor could partly reflect recovery/dating availability of pottery rather than a measured loss of formal diversity. Substantively this is the first decoupling of two pottery-variability components that otherwise co-move strongly (Spearman rho = +0.80 between their century changes): decorative variability expands as vessel-form variability contracts, alongside a decline in the Belau/Woserin pollen openness index from 2.58 to 1.70 (context only).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded time_series_data.csv (3601 x 36, annual CE -4100..-500) and capital.csv (39 x 12 + group, decimal-comma parsed, 100-year CE -4300..-500); established that time_series is derived from capital (exact identity of all 12 Z pairs at the 37 aligned century anchors) and that *_inter is exact piecewise-linear interpolation of the century anchors. 2) Three-way consistency check (canonical *_inter vs raw anchors vs capital Zkeverz/ZKeform): max abs deviation 0.0 everywhere; showed a trailing 100-yr bin mean of *_inter deviates up to 0.93 Z and a centred window up to 0.33 Z from the anchor, so the anchor (century) values are used with no re-binning or re-standardisation. 3) Built century tables on both bases with an assert on ascending-CE (forward-in-time) order; growth = century-to-century first difference (= 100 x annual interpolated slope). 4) PRIMARY strict sign rule Delta_Dec > 0 AND Delta_Form < 0, scanned forward; single hit on both bases at 1700 BCE, attributed to the later century of the 1800 BCE -> 1700 BCE transition. 5) Significance by empirical percentiles/sd of each series' own change distribution, rank of the joint statistic, a bivariate Mahalanobis test on the (Delta_Dec, Delta_Form) pair, and an alignment-breaking permutation test (10,036 permutations), with the honest note that the sign coincidence alone is unremarkable. 6) Sensitivity ladder: 5 magnitude thresholds, 2 sd thresholds, weak/tie rule, two single-sided variants, both bases (12 non-lag variants -> 12/12 1700 BCE), plus rolling-mean (w=2,3 trailing/centred) and annual OLS slope-change constructions reported as onset-lag/acceleration diagnostics only. 7) Earlier near-miss enumeration to secure 'first'. 8) Secondary reversal-of-trend corroboration, plateau/floor diagnostics for assumption A4, and optional pollen context. sub_hypo.text: The first century in which pottery decoration variability increases while pottery form variability decreases is 1700–1600 BCE, assigned to the later endpoint of the 1800 BCE to 1700 BCE transition.

sub_hypo.text: The 1800 BCE to 1700 BCE transition is the largest opposite-signed pottery-variability swing among all 38 century-to-century transitions.

sub_hypo.text: No earlier century qualifies, and identifying 1700 BCE as the first decoupling is robust across all 12 non-lag design variants.

sub_hypo.text: The first decoupling combines a reversal of the form trend with an acceleration of the existing decoration increase, despite strong overall co-movement.

sub_hypo.relations: Form's century change reverses from +0.15 to -1.87 Z, while the decoration increase accelerates approximately 13-fold. Across century changes, the two components otherwise co-move strongly, with Spearman rho = +0.80.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Pottery Decoration diversity and Pottery Form diversity first move in opposite directions in the century 1700-1600 BCE (century beginning CE -1700; Late Neolithic, capital.csv group = LN), at the step from the preceding century 1800 BCE (CE -1800). There Pottery Decoration (Zkeverz / PotteryDecoration_inter) rises significantly from Z = -0.48 to Z = +0.97 (Delta = +1.45 Z, +0.0145 Z/yr, 3.5 sd of its own century-to-century change distribution), while Pottery Form (ZKeform / PotteryForm_inter) simultaneously falls from Z = +0.74 to Z = -1.13 (Delta = -1.87 Z, -0.0187 Z/yr, 3.4 sd) - a 3.32 Z opposite-signed swing and the largest of all 38 century-to-century transitions (rank 1/38; bivariate Mahalanobis distance 5.89, empirical p ~ 0.026). It is the FIRST such century: none of the 25 earlier transitions from 4300 BCE onward satisfies the rule and none comes close - on every earlier century where decoration rose, form did not decline at all (closest +0.01 Z at 2200 BCE), and on every earlier century where form declined, decoration did not rise (closest -0.04 Z at 2000 BCE). The event is a genuine direction reversal for form (+0.15 to -1.87) plus a ~13-fold acceleration of an existing decoration increase, and is unanimous across all 12 design variants (both time bases, magnitude thresholds 0.05-0.5 Z, 0.5/1 sd thresholds, tie-inclusive rule); the only other partially qualifying century is 1000 BCE, 700 years later (Delta Dec +0.56 with form flat at its floor), so 'first' is unambiguous. Under the alternative convention naming the earlier endpoint of the transition the same event is 1800 BCE (CE -1800); smoothing/acceleration constructions spread the apparent onset over 1800-1600 BCE and are onset-lag diagnostics only. Because PotteryForm sits at its floor value (-1.13) in 16 of 39 centuries and both series show long exact plateaus (13 of 38 transitions are no-change for both), the defensible claim is about within-series change rather than absolute diversity or cross-series level comparison, and the fall of PotteryForm to the floor could partly reflect recovery/dating availability of pottery rather than a measured loss of formal diversity. Substantively this is the first decoupling of two pottery-variability components that otherwise co-move strongly (Spearman rho = +0.80 between their century changes): decorative variability expands as vessel-form variability contracts, alongside a decline in the Belau/Woserin pollen openness index from 2.58 to 1.70 (context only).
